question: Neeraj Chopra first set the senior national record during the 2016 South Asian Games held at __________.
solution:
The correct answer is **__Guwahati__.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Neeraj ​​Chopra

 
 
• **Neeraj ​​Chopra set a new personal best at the athletics finals** at the 2016 South Asian Games in Guwahati on February 9.
 
• He won gold with a throw of 82.23 metres, however he fell short of the** 83-meter Olympic qualifying threshold. **
 
• That month, he also started working out with **Australian instructor Gary Calvert**.
 
• Interestingly, **Neeraj Chopra's personal best isn't the 87.58m throw **that won him the gold medal at the Olympics, despite how significant it may have been.
 
• It actually **barely enters the top 10**.
 
• The best throw by **Neeraj Chopra was 89.94 metres**, which he made on June 30, 2022, at the** Stockholm Diamond League in Sweden. **
 
• In the **javelin throw,** Indian track and field athlete** Neeraj Chopra **is the current Olympic champion as well as the world championship silver medalist.
 
• He is the first athlete from **Asia to win the men's javelin throw gold medal** at the Olympics.​
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• ​​​A** multi-sport competition conducted every four years **for athletes from South Asia is called the South Asian Games (SAG or SA Games), formerly known as the** South Asian Federation Games** (SAFG or SAF Games).
 
• The **South Asian Games of 2019 are comprised of 27 games.**
 
• In 1984, Kathmandu, Nepal, served as the host city for the first South Asian Games.
 
• With the exception of 1986, which was a year of the** Commonwealth Games and the Asian Games,** they were held every year from **1984 to 1987.**
 
• **Bangladesh, Bhutan, India, the Maldives, Nepal, Pakistan, and Sri Lanka **are the other six members of the SAOC.
 
• **Afghanistan first took part in the SAF Games **in 2004 and eventually quit the SAOC after competing in the 2016 event.
